newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants to try Zaire envoy over car accident.
newsitem.headline: France wants to try Zaire envoy over car accident.

text.p: France has formally asked Zaire to lift the diplomatic immunity of its ambassador to Paris so that he can be tried for running over two French boys with his car, killing them.
Diplomatic sources said France's envoy in Kinshasa had delivered a formal request from Foreign Minister Herve de Charette to the Zairean government.
The letter was released to reporters after de Charette met the mothers of the dead boys at the foreign ministry.
The mothers are campaigning to bring envoy Ramazani Baya to trial over the accident, which occurred exactly a month ago.
A car driven by Baya hit the two boys on a pedestrian crossing in the Riviera resort of Menton. Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killed instantly and Ronald Lehartel, 12, died a week later in hospital.
French police have said that Baya, on his way to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko at his nearby villa, was driving at 100 kph (60 mph) in a 45-kph (30-mph) zone.

"You certainly understand why it would be unacceptable for the families, which have been seriously affected, if justice were not allowed to be done in such a tragic case, whatever the nationality of the person who caused the accident," de Charette said in the letter to Zairean Foreign Minister Kititwa Tumansi.
De Charette wrote that Baya was also deeply affected by the accident and had reacted with dignity by offering to renounce his immunity.
But under the Vienna Convention a diplomat may not renounce his immunity. Only the state which appointed him can lift it, de Charette said.
